interventions.name: Box Breathing
interventions.purpose: A paced breathing experience for moments of physical activation, tension or scattered attention. It gives the user a predictable rhythm and a steady attentional anchor without requiring them to force calm.
interventions.psychoeducation: Slow, structured breathing can support autonomic regulation and increase heart-rate variability. Evidence is stronger for slow-paced breathing generally than for the exact 4-4-4-4 pattern.
flow: Finish or hand off to grounding
interventions.visualAudio: Deep emerald volumetric glass square; expansion travels around four edges with no sudden flashes. Quiet low-frequency bed, soft directional cues and warm optional narration; static edge highlighting for reduced motion.
interventions.upgrade: The breathing object is both pacer and progress cue. Holds can be removed without restarting, guidance changes in place, and success is breathing comfort or usable attention rather than a required feeling of calm.
interventions.evidenceGrade: A for slow-paced breathing; C for the exact branded pattern
interventions.limits: Do not imply that the exact four-part ratio is superior. Stop or remove holds if dizziness, air hunger or respiratory discomfort occurs.

interventions.name: Progressive Muscle Relaxation
interventions.purpose: A body-led experience for prominent muscular tension when safe tensing or release-only attention is possible. It helps the user notice the contrast between tension and release and choose what their body can comfortably soften.
interventions.psychoeducation: Progressive muscle relaxation has evidence for reducing stress and anxiety in adults. The useful mechanism is learning the contrast between tension and release, not forcing every muscle to relax.
flow: Check pain, injury and movement comfort
Choose Immediate, Standard, Supported or release-only
interventions.visualAudio: Neutral inclusive body silhouette with user-selectable regions; warm points gather during tension and dissolve on release. Slow low pulse, breath-safe cues and precise narration; list and tap alternatives replace the body map when needed.
interventions.upgrade: Suitability is checked before tensing, every region can be skipped, release-only remains a full pathway, and the outcome records where tension changed rather than demanding total relaxation.
interventions.evidenceGrade: A for PMR generally; C for this interaction system
interventions.limits: Evidence covers varied PMR protocols and populations. Avoid painful or injured areas and use release-only when tensing is unsuitable.

interventions.name: 5-4-3-2-1 Grounding
interventions.purpose: An eyes-open sensory orientation experience for overwhelm, disconnection or narrowed attention. It rebuilds contact with the immediate environment one sense at a time without asking the user to analyse why they feel this way.
interventions.psychoeducation: Grounding uses present sensory information to redirect attention toward the here and now. The exact 5-4-3-2-1 sequence is widely used, but direct efficacy research on that specific sequence remains limited.
flow: Check immediate safety and orient eyes open
Taste one or use a neutral alternative
interventions.visualAudio: A quiet world progressively rebuilds through light, ripple, wave, wisp and droplet layers. Each sense has one tactile sound identity; narration is optional and every gesture has a large tap target.
interventions.upgrade: Discovery replaces a checklist: the environment visibly returns as senses are named. Counts can be shortened, inaccessible senses skipped, and success is orientation rather than symptom disappearance.
interventions.limits: The review notes that grounding has lacked agreed definitions and efficacy studies. Never present this as proven treatment for dissociation or trauma.

interventions.name: Thought or Fact
interventions.purpose: A private evidence review for distressing thoughts that have begun to feel certain. It helps the user separate observable facts from interpretation, prediction and catastrophe while keeping the feeling itself valid.
interventions.psychoeducation: Cognitive approaches can reduce anxiety and depression by helping people examine interpretations and generate more balanced alternatives. This is a brief sorting tool, not a diagnostic test or a verdict on whether a person is right.
flow: Separate fact, interpretation, prediction or catastrophe
Choose next action or safe experiment
interventions.visualAudio: A softened private evidence chamber: dark amber glass, movable evidence cards and one illuminated clarity line. Sparse paper movement and optional measured narration; no courtroom verdict imagery.
interventions.upgrade: The experience makes uncertainty visible, prevents forced positive thinking and offers Test the Prediction only when a real-world question is safely testable.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B for CBT/cognitive change; C for this brief standalone sorter
interventions.limits: Do not use to challenge trauma memories, abuse disclosures, delusional or paranoid beliefs, or immediate danger. Evidence is for broader CBT packages, not this screen sequence alone.

interventions.name: Urge Surfing
interventions.purpose: A choice-window experience for a strong urge that can be observed safely without immediate action. It helps the user notice that urge intensity and behaviour are separate, creating room for a deliberate next choice.
interventions.psychoeducation: Mindfulness practice may weaken the link between craving and action even when the urge does not immediately disappear. The goal is a more available choice, not a promise that every urge will pass within a fixed time.
flow: Name the urge without storing detail
Finish, leave the trigger or seek support
interventions.visualAudio: A dark oceanic wave responds to a simple intensity trace; the line remains honest when flat or rising. Low tide texture and optional sparse voice; static trace and automatic pacing are equivalent routes.
interventions.upgrade: Safety precedes immersion, duration is a user-selected pause rather than biology, and unchanged or stronger urges remain valid outcomes. The standout measure is choice availability.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B for mindfulness and craving-response decoupling; C for this brief wave interaction
interventions.limits: Results for brief app-based mindfulness are mixed. This is not suitable when an urge involves immediate danger, overdose risk, self-harm or harm to others.

interventions.name: Then What?
interventions.purpose: A bounded coping-appraisal pathway for a feared future frozen at its worst frame. It continues the timeline far enough to identify coping, support and what remains intact without promising that the feared event is harmless or unlikely.
interventions.psychoeducation: Cognitive change and perspective-taking can reduce emotional impact by changing how a situation is understood. This pathway tests coping beyond the worst frame; it is not reassurance and does not establish what will happen.
flow: Check danger, activation and reassurance looping
Name what it has come to mean
Map first person and first resource
Decide whether action is needed now
Save the coping route and stop
interventions.visualAudio: A cinematic strip begins as one frozen frame and opens into five bounded illuminated nodes. Each node appears once with a soft click; no endless zoom, branching catastrophe or dramatic crescendo.
interventions.upgrade: The system detects when analysis is becoming reassurance-seeking and routes to Grounding or Urge Surfing. It stores a coping route, never a catastrophe rehearsal.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B for cognitive change/perspective-taking; C for this bounded standalone sequence
interventions.limits: Not for immediate danger, acute panic, trauma re-experiencing, impaired reality testing or repetitive certainty-seeking. Broader CBT evidence does not prove the exact sequence.

interventions.name: Ignition Point
interventions.purpose: A low-pressure activation pathway for low reward expectancy, flatness or reduced motivation. It helps the user choose one reachable source of Pleasure, Mastery, Connection or Dream and make contact with it before waiting to feel motivated.
interventions.psychoeducation: Behavioural activation works by increasing meaningful contact between a person and their environment. A small action can be worthwhile before mood changes, so success is engagement with value or reward rather than instant happiness.
flow: Check whether rest or safety is the real need
Choose Pleasure, Mastery, Connection or Dream
interventions.visualAudio: Four premium energy constellations orbit a small ignition core, each with a distinct material and gentle pulse. Warm rise without triumphal music; optional narration uses invitational language.
interventions.upgrade: The permanent Dream pathway protects future-directed meaning alongside immediate reward. The system learns only user-confirmed reachability and worthwhileness, not hidden mood labels.
interventions.evidenceGrade: A for behavioural activation packages; C for the four-pathway branded selector
interventions.limits: Evidence is mainly from depression treatment protocols delivered over time. One micro-action should not be described as treatment or guaranteed mood improvement.

interventions.name: The Happy Bump
interventions.purpose: A completion-led behavioural activation sequence for flatness, low energy or difficulty getting started. It stacks movement, self-selected music, hydration, a safe five-minute walk, social approach, mastery, positive reflection and values-led action.
interventions.psychoeducation: Behavioural activation can improve low mood by increasing contact with rewarding, meaningful and mastery-building activity before motivation arrives. Movement, social connection, positive reflection and values-led action are offered as accessible supports, not guaranteed mood treatments.
flow: Connect during the walk or deliberately skip
Choose a wellbeing area and complete one low-effort step
Plan one productive, enjoyable or relaxing activity
Replay and optionally save the combination
interventions.visualAudio: One living emerald-and-gold curve gains pulse, travel, a returning signal and a stable resting shape as actions accumulate. Sparse causal tones and optional haptics mark only meaningful transitions; reduced motion preserves every state change without animation.
interventions.upgrade: The intervention makes a sequence of completed actions feel like one continuous object rather than a checklist. It ends with an evidence-informed life direction and a concrete next activity, records the user's actual before-and-after state without promising improvement, and remembers only broad preferences.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B+ for behavioural activation; mixed and component-specific evidence for the combined sequence
interventions.limits: The combined branded sequence has not been independently tested. Movement must remain safe and capacity-matched; music, hydration and social contact do not guarantee a mood shift. The six wellbeing areas are evidence-informed domains, not a definitive universal ranking.

interventions.name: Change the Scene
interventions.purpose: An environmental interruption for flatness or inertia that is being reinforced by the current setting. It helps the user make one safe change of position, view or place so a different next behaviour becomes available.
interventions.psychoeducation: Stable contexts can cue automatic behaviour, while a context change can interrupt those cues and create a window for a different choice. Evidence supports the broader context-discontinuity principle, not this exact short intervention.
flow: Check that movement and the destination are safe
Choose turn, doorway, room or outside
Notice what behaviour is now available
Finish or continue with an action pathway
interventions.visualAudio: One physical portal cuts through a muted scene; parallax and light temperature change only after the transition. A single threshold sound and environmental bed replace motivational music.
interventions.upgrade: The app checks whether a scene change is realistic and does not claim the new place must improve mood. The system remembers useful scene types only after repeated user confirmation.
interventions.limits: The cited context-discontinuity evidence concerns longer-term habit contexts, not momentary mood shifts. Keep claims modest and never direct users into unsafe environments.

interventions.name: Test the Prediction
interventions.purpose: A real-world behavioural experiment for a specific negative prediction that can be tested safely, ethically and proportionately. It replaces imagined certainty with direct observation while allowing confirming, mixed and unanswered results.
interventions.psychoeducation: Behavioural experiments can help people compare a prediction with observable experience. Evidence suggests benefit within anxiety treatment, but results must be read fairly and should never be designed to prove the user wrong.
flow: Run the eligibility and safety screen
Record confirming, disconfirming, mixed or unanswered evidence
interventions.visualAudio: Two balanced glass panels hold Prediction and Observation with a neutral bridge between them. Evidence particles move without winning colours, fanfare or scales that imply disconfirmation is the correct result.
interventions.upgrade: Eligibility blocks medical, legal, dangerous, coercive and reality-testing use. All result types have equal visual dignity and can hand back to Thought or Fact for fair interpretation.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B for behavioural experiments in anxiety treatment; C for this standalone digital path
interventions.limits: The review found methodological limitations and studied behavioural experiments inside treatment. Never create high-stakes, unsafe or boundary-violating tests.

interventions.name: Open Channel
interventions.purpose: A relational re-entry experience after safe connection has been interrupted by silence, withdrawal, cancellation or shame. It helps the user choose and review one honest bridge without requiring a reply or accessing contacts.
interventions.psychoeducation: Interventions that increase access to people or address barriers to connection can improve social contact and perceived connection. One message is only a bridge, not a guaranteed repair or cure for loneliness.
flow: Check safety, consent and no-contact boundaries
Choose Signal, Reopen, Repair, Ask or Presence
Draft in the user's own voice
Complete outside the app or deliberately decline
Record the decision, not the other person's response
interventions.visualAudio: Two quiet points separated by fractured space; a bridge forms segment by segment only after the user approves language. Restrained connection tone, no message-send sound unless the app actually sends something.
interventions.upgrade: The system separates connection from contact-at-any-cost, makes not contacting a valid outcome, and never reads contacts, sends messages or fabricates a response.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B for broader social-connection interventions; C for a single digital re-entry prompt
interventions.limits: Intervention effects vary and much evidence concerns multi-session programmes. Do not use for abuse, coercion, unsafe former partners or when no contact has been requested.

interventions.name: Countermove
interventions.purpose: A graded opposite-direction experience for withdrawal or emotion-driven avoidance when the pull is neither protective nor restorative. It creates the smallest behaviour that widens life while allowing the feeling to remain present.
interventions.psychoeducation: Behavioural activation increases meaningful interaction with the environment, and specific action plans can help close the gap between intention and behaviour. A small directional move can count before mood changes.
flow: Check whether it protects, restores or avoids
Make it lighter or change direction
interventions.visualAudio: A matte sphere sits in a soft gravitational field; one selected trajectory bends by the chosen degree. Low hum, directional tone and subtle haptic confirmation; reduced motion shows a static before-and-after line.
interventions.upgrade: Function is checked before action so safety and genuine rest are never mislabeled as avoidance. The trajectory engine scales one mechanism without ranking stronger moves as better.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B for behavioural activation and implementation intentions; C for the graded trajectory interface
interventions.limits: Evidence comes from broader interventions, not the 5/20/45-degree metaphor. Do not oppose behaviour that is protective, restorative or required for safety.

interventions.name: Pulse Shift
interventions.purpose: A capacity-matched movement experience for flatness, heaviness, fogginess or physical inertia. It creates a small amount of usable activation and then directs it toward a real-life action without becoming exercise coaching.
interventions.psychoeducation: A single bout of exercise is associated on average with modest improvements in mood and anxiety, but responses vary widely. Here the aim is simply to make a little more movement available, not to prescribe intensity or promise a mood lift.
flow: Check pain, dizziness, instability and genuine need for rest
Choose lying, seated, standing or already moving
Direct it toward one real action
interventions.visualAudio: A near-static body field receives one travelling pulse that grows only to the selected capacity. Percussive texture stays soft and tempo-stable; captions, seated alternatives and tap pacing are native.
interventions.upgrade: The pathway starts from position and capacity rather than a fitness norm. Rest, no change and deliberate stopping are valid outcomes, and concerning symptoms route away immediately.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B for acute exercise affect; C for micro-dose graded activation
interventions.limits: The meta-analysis found substantial heterogeneity and typically studied exercise bouts, not tiny movements. This is not medical or exercise advice.

interventions.name: Reroute
interventions.purpose: A brief orientation and attentional-redirection experience for genuine distress when a longer grounding exercise is unlikely to be usable. It gives attention one safe, absorbing destination while preserving the option to return to the problem later.
interventions.psychoeducation: Distraction can reduce emotional impact in some contexts, but its usefulness depends on the emotion, timing and purpose. Reroute is a deliberate short-term shift of attention, not suppression or a claim that the problem no longer matters.
flow: Check immediate danger and urgent practical action
Choose Social, Sensory, Familiar, Active or Absorbing destination
Return, repeat once or choose another mechanism
interventions.visualAudio: Visual interference clears around one stable point, then a single route opens through the field. Directional sound follows the route; reduced-motion mode swaps travelling lines for progressive contrast.
interventions.upgrade: The tool distinguishes deliberate redirection from avoidance, asks whether attention actually entered, and hands to Next Easiest Step when the destination fits but the first action is unclear.
interventions.limits: The meta-analysis found strategy and context differences; attentional deployment was not uniformly effective. Do not use when urgent safety or practical action is required.

interventions.name: Next Easiest Step
interventions.purpose: An executive-friction reducer for tasks that feel unclear, effortful, distracting or too large. It converts a general intention into one observable physical action that can begin now or be taken outside the app.
interventions.psychoeducation: Specific action plans can improve goal attainment by linking intention to a concrete response. The useful target is a visible next behaviour, not a perfect plan or a judgment about motivation.
flow: Check that it can begin quickly
Take the step outside the app
Record complete, partial or could not start
Hand off to Ignition Point or Signal Lock if useful
interventions.visualAudio: A dense cloud of task fragments compresses into one bright physical tile. Soft mechanical clicks mark simplification; no ticking clock unless the user chooses a timed handoff.
interventions.upgrade: Barrier-specific compression avoids generic advice. Could not start becomes information that either reduces the step again or changes mechanism rather than a failure state.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B for implementation intentions; C for task-compression micro-intervention
interventions.limits: If-then planning evidence does not establish an optimal 20-second start rule. Keep the action user-editable and do not score productivity.

interventions.name: Signal Lock
interventions.purpose: A task-scaffolding and bounded sprint system for a chosen task that is startable but vulnerable to interruption. It clarifies the target, contains predictable distractions and supports deliberate focus without pretending to control the device.
interventions.psychoeducation: Reducing interruption costs and using deliberate time-management strategies can support task accuracy, resumption and wellbeing. Evidence does not show that one branded timer length is universally best.
flow: Name and test a concrete target
Scaffold first action, materials and finish line
Calibrate outcome without a productivity score
interventions.visualAudio: A radar field closes onto one lockable target; interruptions become parked points outside the reticle. Restrained pulse and optional finish cue; static timer, hidden-time and screen-reader modes are equivalent.
interventions.upgrade: The sprint begins only after the target is startable, device-control claims are honest, time pressure is evaluated rather than assumed helpful, and distractions remain private and removable.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B for interruption mitigation/time management; C for the exact sprint engine
interventions.limits: Much interruption evidence is laboratory-based and time-management evidence is correlational or heterogeneous. Do not claim the timer treats attention disorders.

interventions.name: Tomorrow Parking Lot
interventions.purpose: A low-light cognitive-offloading experience for unfinished responsibilities being rehearsed at bedtime. It captures one item outside the night and defers decisions, reminders and action planning to a separate daytime review.
interventions.psychoeducation: In one small sleep-laboratory study, writing a specific bedtime to-do list was associated with faster sleep onset than writing about completed activities. This supports offloading as a useful option, not a guarantee of sleep.
flow: Check whether the item is urgent or safety-critical
Slide or tap the item outside the night
Offer Night Channel only with consent
Review, edit or delete in daytime
interventions.visualAudio: Near-black indigo field with one luminous note moving beyond a quiet horizon. A single soft containment sound; no celebration, reminder ping or bright completion state.
interventions.upgrade: The night flow has only two active screens, sensitive text is local and explicitly saved, urgent items escape before sealing, and no hidden categorisation or reminder is created.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B-: one small randomised laboratory study plus cognitive-offloading rationale
interventions.limits: The study included 57 healthy young adults and used five minutes of writing. Do not promise sleep onset or generalise to clinical insomnia without caution.

interventions.name: Night Channel
interventions.purpose: A low-effort audio destination for bedtime rumination when the user wants something sufficiently interesting to drift into. It supports familiar replay, gentle curiosity or fuller capture without creating another task to finish.
interventions.psychoeducation: Music may improve subjective sleep quality for some adults, while effects on objective sleep and other audio formats are less certain. Choose content that feels settling; Night Channel does not guarantee sleep.
flow: Choose Familiar Replay, Continuing Story, Gentle Curiosity, Gentle Conversation or Fictional World
Select native Mentication audio or an honest external handoff
Stop deliberately with no night rating
interventions.visualAudio: Distant broadcast channels float in a near-black indigo space and resolve into one soft frequency line. Native audio can fade; external media remains under its own app's controls. No autoplay feed.
interventions.upgrade: Familiar Replay includes a known song, show, video, podcast or audiobook without voice cloning. Source boundaries are explicit, content is finite, and Mentication never simulates control of an external service.
interventions.evidenceGrade: B for music listening; C/insufficient for podcasts, audiobooks and the branded channel system
interventions.limits: Subjective music findings are more positive than objective measures, and evidence for general-population sleep is mixed. External content quality and autoplay are outside Mentication's control.
